Indications: Any wound type but especially sloughy, necrotic, and malodorous wounds, including: pressure ulcers, leg ulcers, diabetic ulcers, surgical wounds, burns, graft sites, infected wounds, cavity wounds and sinuses
Mechanism of Action: Debrides necrotic tissue; can be used in dressings or directly into cavities.
Clinical Evidence: Inhibition of in vitro formation of clinically important Gram-positive bacteria biofilms [155]. Blistering and cellulitis on a type 2 diabetic patient; paediatric burn; foot ulceration; grade 5 sacral wound [154]

Description: Knitted viscose mesh dressing impregnated with 100% manuka honey
Indications: Granulating or shallow wounds, good when debriding or de-sloughing small areas of necrotic or sloughy tissue
Mechanism of Action: Creates a moist healing environment, eliminates wound odour, and provides antibacterial action
Clinical Evidence: Overgranulated grade 3 and 4 pressure ulcers; extensive leg cellulitis; venous ulcer; chronic wound infections; necrotic foot [154]

Description: Reinforced alginate dressing impregnated with 100% manuka honey
Indications: Pressure, leg and diabetic ulcers, surgical wounds, burns, graft sites and infected wounds. Ideal for wetter wounds
Mechanism of Action: Absorbs exudate. Debrides, removes slough, and reduces bacterial load

Description: Reinforced alginate ribbon impregnated with 100% manuka honey
Indications: Cavities, sinuses, pressure ulcers, leg ulcers, diabetic ulcers, surgical wounds, burns, graft sites, and infected wounds
Mechanism of Action: Absorb exudates. Debrides, removes slough, and reduces bacterial load

Description: Medical-grade manuka honey added to the hydrocolloid
Mechanism of Action: Kills bacteria, suppresses inflammation, and stimulates the growth of cells to promote healthy skin around the stoma

Description: Combined hydrogel and honey (30%) pad on a strong fixation layer
Indications: Chronic wounds, such as: pressure ulcers; superficial and partial-thickness burns; venous, arterial, and diabetic ulcers.
Mechanism of Action: Exudate absorption. Donates moisture to rehydrate dry tissue. Antibacterial properties. Helps to maintain a moist wound environment

Description: Sterile, semi-permeable hydrogel dressing containing 30% honey with vitamin C and E, as well as an acrylic polymer gel and water, with a polyurethane film backing
Indications: Low to moderate exuding wounds, including:chronic wounds (pressure ulcers, venous and diabetic ulcers), superficial and acute wounds (cuts, abrasions and donor sites), superficial and partial-thickness burns (first- and second-degree), fungating wounds, acute wounds, e.g., donor sites, surgical wounds, cuts and abrasions
Mechanism of Action: Donates moisture to rehydrate dry tissue. Antibacterial properties. Helps to maintain a moist wound environment
Clinical Evidence: Paediatric minor burns and scalds [162]. Fungating wounds [163]

Description: Ointment with 48% medical-grade honey, medical-grade hypoallergenic lanolin, oils, and vitamins
Indications: Superficial, acute, and chronic wounds. Superficial and partial-thickness burns. Fungating wounds (to help deodorise and debride). Colonised acute wounds and (postoperative) surgical wounds
Mechanism of Action: Aids debridement and reduce bacterial colonisation

Description: Wound dressing made with 100% Leptospermum scoparium sterile honey from New Zealand. Non-adherent impregnated gauze
Indications: Leg and pressure ulcers, first- and second-degree burns, diabetic foot ulcers, surgical and trauma wounds
Mechanism of Action: Osmotic activity that promotes autolytic debridement and helps maintain a moist wound environment
Clinical Evidence: Burn management [165]. Difficult-to-debride wounds [166]. Necrotic pressure ulcer; recurrent venous leg ulceration [167]

Indications: All types of wounds with low to moderate exudate, including: deep, sinus, necrotic, infected, surgic and malodorous wounds®
Mechanism of Action: Creates an antibacterial environment (MGO). Autolytic debridement on sloughy and necrotic tissue. Removes malodour. Provides a moist environment.
Clinical Evidence: Wound healing [169]; prevention of catheter-associated infections in haemodialysis patients [170]

Description: Calcium alginate dressing impregnated with 100% medical-grade manuka honey
Indications: Moderately to heavily exuding wounds such as: diabetic foot ulcers, leg ulcers, pressure ulcers (partial- and full-thickness), first- and second-degree partial-thickness burns, donor sites and traumatic or surgical wounds.
Mechanism of Action: Promotes a moisture-balanced environment. Osmotic potential draws fluid through the wound to the surface. Low pH of 3.5–4.5.

Description: Barrier cream containing 30% medical-grade manuka honey
Indications: Use to protect skin from breakdown (e.g., skin damaged by irradiation treatment or in wet areas due to incontinence). Additionally, to prevent damage caused by shear and friction
Clinical Evidence: Treatment for intertrigo in large skin folds [174]

Description: Antibacterial wound gel: 80% medical-grade manuka honey with natural waxes and oils
Indications: Surface wounds with low to moderate exudate and partial- and full-thickness wounds, including burns, cuts, grazes, and eczema wounds
Mechanism of Action: Creates a moist, low-pH environment. Cleans the wound through osmotic effect. Reduces the risk of infection (MGO)
Clinical Evidence: Reduction in incidence of wound infection after microvascular free tissue reconstruction [176]

Description: Antimicrobial wound gel utilising bioengineered honey to deliver Reactive Oxygen® (RO™)
Indications: Infected, chronic (diabetic foot, pressure, and leg ulcers) and acute (surgical, traumatic and abrasions wounds, cuts, burns, donor and recipient sites) wounds
Mechanism of Action: Controlled release of hydrogen peroxide release for antimicrobial activity. Promotes debridement and new tissue growth
Clinical Evidence: Prevention of caesareanwound infection; prevention/eradication of bacterial colonies in dressing oncology long vascular lines; ulcers, surgical wounds and trauma wounds [178,179,180]. In vitro activity against biofilm-producing clinical bacterial isolates [181]
